purpose: Experiments that shaped the Java Access Bridge adapter and the environment facts behind every NOT_RUN entry. Run by hand on the same Windows 11 host as the functional reports. The regression runner repeats the ones marked repeatedByRunner.

host.cpu: 12th Gen Intel Core i7-1255U, 12 logical processors

installedJavaRuntimes.version: Eclipse Adoptium 23.0.2+7 (bundled with an Eclipse IDE installation)

notInstalled.policy: No runtime was downloaded or installed for this work. Every combination that needs one is NOT_RUN.

bridgeIdentity.tool: a throwaway Java program that called JabBridge directly

observations.note: Reached through the JDK 17 WindowsAccessBridge-64.dll. getVersionInfo reported 23.0.2 for the JVM side.

observations.targetJvm: Oracle JDK 17.0.10 x64, Swing, bridge not enabled
observations.note: Three bridge-enabled windows were found among 26 visible top-level windows. This one was not.

bridgeIdentity.conclusion: The JVM identifier is the handle of the bridge window inside the target JVM. Bounds are physical pixels on this 125 % display for Java 17 and 23.

swingModalClick.fixture: tests/fixtures/swing-awt/FrameworkFixture.java, JButton "Open fixture modal" whose listener calls JDialog.setVisible(true)

firstImplementation.nextRequest: listWindows ended as TIMEOUT after 10 s and the session was retired
firstImplementation.finding: doAccessibleActions returned non-zero after the library gave up waiting. The reply buffer of the library is not initialized, so the value carried no information.

currentImplementation.afterTheFixtureClosedTheDialog: listWindows answered OK in the same session

swingModalClick.source: JDK 17 src.zip, jdk.accessibility/com/sun/java/accessibility/internal/AccessBridge.java: doAccessibleActions runs AccessibleAction.doAccessibleAction through InvocationUtils.invokeAndWait, which posts an InvocationEvent and calls lock.wait() without a timeout (lines 4154-4182 and 7282-7300). javax.swing.AbstractButton.doClick fires the action listeners synchronously.
swingModalClick.conclusion: JAB_PROVIDER_LIMITATION. A listener that opens a modal dialog keeps the bridge thread of the JVM blocked until the dialog closes.
swingModalClick.repeatedByRunner: modalOpenedByInvoke and exitWhileTargetSilent in the Swing rows.

awtTextInput.result: setTextContents returned FALSE within 6 ms and value.txt kept its content
awtTextInput.source: AccessBridge.setTextContents returns false unless the context is an AccessibleEditableText (line 4195). java.awt.TextComponent.AccessibleAWTTextComponent implements AccessibleText only.

awtButton.result: doAccessibleActions returned TRUE within 20 ms and count.txt rose by one in every repetition, on both agents
awtButton.source: java.awt.Button.AccessibleAWTButton.doAccessibleAction posts an ActionEvent to the event queue (Button.java lines 631-642), so the call returns before the listener runs.
awtButton.harnessNote: An ad-hoc reader that opened count.txt at the moment of the reply made the fixture's atomic replace fail on Windows. The fixture now retries the replace.
awtButton.repeatedByRunner: invokeAndDuplicateRequest, replacement, modalOpenedByInvoke in the AWT rows.

withoutLibrary.reason: No WindowsAccessBridge-32.dll was found in the Windows system directory or a registered Java installation.

msaaWinForms.tool: tools/Probe-MsaaChildren.ps1 (IAccessible through oleacc.dll, no UI Automation and no Agent)

listSelection.finding: The call returned and the SelectedIndexChanged handler of the application did not run.

tabActivation.finding: The second page became the visible one: the DataGridView and TreeView below were reachable afterwards.

msaaWinForms.conclusion: MSAA shows the ListBox items and tabs that UI Automation gives no usable runtime ID for. Each is a simple element named only by its parent window and its position. DataGridView rows are objects without an identity interface, and two fetches of the same row give two COM objects. MSAA therefore offers no identity stronger than position for these elements.
